headline: PPWR names chemicals in three rows and reaches it in five — but regulates the buyer of 11.3% of its output on 82 of 89 rows
body:
Read row by row, the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation touches chemicals manufacture lightly: three of its 89 rows name the sector, and five more reach it. The sector the file actually regulates is plastics converting — 44 rows name it and a further 38 reach it, 82 of the file's 89 rows in total.

The FIGARO input-output table is what connects the two. Chemicals is the single largest supplier to plastics converting, providing 21.6% of the converting sector's total inputs in the EU view. Run the same table the other way and rubber & plastics is chemicals' largest intermediate customer, taking 11.3% of the chemicals sector's total output — more than farming (5.6%), construction (4.5%) or pharmaceuticals (3.9%).

The packaging regulation names plastics converting in 44 measures, including the recyclability grades, the recycled-content minimums, and the format prohibitions. The chemicals sector appears in the regulation's own text only in the substance provisions. The input-output data adds a second route: 21.6% of plastics converting's inputs come from the chemicals sector, so measures that change what converters may produce also change what converters buy. The finding computes that route: [N] converter-addressed measures whose compliance changes input demand, against a supplier share of 21.6% recorded in the FIGARO table. The register records the named route; the exposure data records the supplied one; the two together are the sector's full position under the regulation.

evidence.notes: Counts are taken across every row in data/ppwr.json: 3 rows carry chem in sectors_named and 5 in sectors_reached; 44 rows carry chem/plastics in sectors_named and 38 in sectors_reached (82 of 89 rows in the file). SUB-01 is one of the three rows naming chem; RCY-01 and RCY-02 are recycled-content minimums that name chem/plastics and reach chem. The two shares are the stored FIGARO figures: C20 (chemicals) at 21.6% of chem/plastics inputs, and C22 (rubber & plastics) at 11.3% of chem customers, both EU view; the comparison customers (A01 5.6%, F 4.5%, C21 3.9%) are the next three rows of the same customer list.

review.q: Draft pending George's edit. One unresolved bracket: '[N] converter-addressed measures whose compliance changes input demand' — the finding body computes 44 rows naming chem/plastics and 82 naming or reaching it, but no count of measures whose compliance changes input demand, so the bracket was left rather than filled.
